entities.summary:
John of Trogir was a Christian saint who served as the bishop of Trogir in the 11th century. He was born in unknown circumstances and died on November 14, 1111. As bishop, John played a significant role in shaping the religious landscape of medieval Croatia.

During his tenure, he oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries, including the Cathedral of St. Lawrence in Trogir. He also established a network of charitable institutions that provided aid to the poor and vulnerable.

John's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he became a revered figure in Croatian history. His devotion to Christianity and commitment to social justice have inspired generations of Croatians, who continue to venerate him as a patron saint.

A striking testament to John's enduring impact is the annual Trogir Festival, which celebrates the city's rich cultural heritage and honors its beloved bishop. Today, John of Trogir remains an important figure in Croatian history, symbolizing the power of faith and compassion.
